chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAllān, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn Yūnus.
That his father wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام asking him about the junub: may he dye himself, or enter janābah while he is dyed? So he wrote: “I do not like that for him.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَا أُحِبُّ: I do not approve; an expression of disapproval
key_terms.مُخْتَضِبٌ: having dye applied; being in a dyed state
key_terms.يَخْتَضِبُ: he applies dye, such as henna, to himself
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: he enters the state of janabah

ai.seo_question: What did Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام say about dyeing while in janabah or becoming junub while dyed?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal question concerning a person in the state of janabah and the use of dye. Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام replied with a statement of disapproval, indicating that he did not approve of this practice. The narration is relevant to rulings of ritual purity.
